title: Milestone 1 — bounded retries, from intention to evidence
subtitle: Baseline: the shared starter. Proposed synchronous library; report viewer is its consumer. D / A / C / I / S / V identify subjects across the six perspectives.

lanes.title: D1 · Recover without losing control
body: Application authors want a transient failure to recover, while callers regain control after a bounded number of calls.
A1 seeks this outcome; D2 enables it.

lanes.title: D2 · Repeat an eligible operation
body: Today: the package has no retry API.
Proposed: Retry Kit invokes a supplied operation until success, an unrelated failure, or the total attempt limit.

lanes.title: D3 · Caller selects failures
body: Only listed Exception types, including subclasses, permit another attempt. An empty list retries nothing.
Constrains D2; protects caller control in D1. Cancellation signals escape.

lanes.title: D4 · Count the first call
body: attempts is a positive integer; bool is invalid. Three attempts means at most three invocations, including the first.
Constrains D2; guarantees the bound in D1.

lanes.title: D5 · Preserve the outcome
body: Return the same successful object. On exhaustion, re-raise the same last exception. An unrelated error escapes immediately.
Constrains D2; protects the caller’s interpretation of success or failure.

lanes.title: A1 · Application author / viewer
body: The author chooses which failures are safe to repeat. The report viewer consumes the library inside its own process.
Retry does not undo operation effects or establish repeat safety.

lanes.title: A2 · Retry Kit
body: Today: importable package scaffold.
Proposed: owns retry admission and repeated invocation. Calls A3 through I3; returns through I2. No service or worker is added.

lanes.title: A3 · Report operation
body: Today: load_report always succeeds.
Proposed example: two failures, then report success. Its readiness and side effects remain caller-owned; library sees only result or exception.

lanes.title: A4 · Python runtime
body: One synchronous call stack in the caller’s process. Standard exception matching selects eligible failures.
No network, background task, persistence, clock, or waiting dependency.

lanes.title: A5 · Distribution / consumer
body: Today: package import and first-call report smoke test.
Proposed: installed consumer exercises public retries, including exhaustion and permission failure. Wheel check retains the installation boundary.

lanes.title: C1 · RetryPolicy
body: No policy exists today. A frozen value validates attempts and exception classes; snapshots the supplied collection as a tuple.
Invalid policy fails before any operation runs.

lanes.title: C2 · retry executor
body: No retry loop exists today. For each allowed attempt, call the operation and return immediately on success.
Catch only policy.retry_on; re-raise at the last attempt.

lanes.title: C3 · Public exports
body: Today: package docstring only.
Proposed: export RetryPolicy and retry; private modules remain implementation details. Type variable retains the operation’s return type.

lanes.title: C4 · Report rehearsal
body: Today: one direct successful read.
Proposed: print three deterministic scenarios: success on read 3; exhaustion on read 2; permission failure on read 1.

lanes.title: C5 · No shared invocation state
body: C2 keeps its counter inside each invocation. Reusing one C1 policy does not carry failures or counts into another call.
No retry schedule is introduced in milestone 1.

lanes.title: I1 · RetryPolicy(attempts, retry_on)
body: attempts: positive int. retry_on: collection of Exception classes. Defaults: one attempt, no eligible exceptions.
Caller supplies choices; C1 validates and freezes them.

lanes.title: I2 · retry(operation, *, policy)
body: Caller supplies a zero-argument callable and validated policy. C2 returns its value or raises its exception.
Validate callable before the loop; do not classify a noncallable input as an operation failure.

lanes.title: I3 · operation() callback
body: Retry Kit calls the caller-owned operation. The callback returns T or raises an exception.
Arguments can be bound with a closure. There is no decorator or async protocol.

lanes.title: I4 · Failure propagation
body: Eligible and attempts remain: another immediate call. Eligible and exhausted: bare re-raise. Unrelated: escapes.
KeyboardInterrupt / SystemExit cannot be eligible policy entries.

lanes.title: I5 · Consumer command
body: uv run --locked python examples/read_report.py
Today: one report line. Proposed: visible result plus call counts for success, exhaustion, and permission error.

lanes.title: S1 · Validated policy
body: Created once by C1; immutable per-instance fields. Snapshot of retry_on prevents caller list mutation changing retry eligibility.
Reuse shares settings, never an attempt counter.

lanes.title: S2 · Attempt ordinal
body: Local integer 1..policy.attempts, advanced only by the loop before invoking I3.
First call is 1. After an eligible failure, the current ordinal decides whether a new call is allowed.

lanes.title: S3 · Current result / failure
body: Success is returned directly. The active exception remains available for bare re-raise; no wrapper replaces it.
Failure history is not retained after the call finishes.

lanes.title: S4 · Report readiness
body: Today: constant report value.
Proposed: each example scenario owns a fresh read counter; readiness is reached on its third call. A permission case always fails.

lanes.title: S5 · No durable retry record
body: Starter has no database or persisted job state. That boundary remains.
Restarting the process starts a new invocation; the library supplies no effect deduplication or recovery log.

lanes.title: V1 · Policy unit checks
body: Reject zero/negative/non-integer attempts and non-Exception classes. Verify tuple snapshot and frozen fields.
Failure signal: invalid inputs run or policy changes after construction.

lanes.title: V2 · Public API acceptance
body: Two failures then success: limit 3 returns the original object after 3 calls; limit 2 raises the second failure after 2 calls.
Enter through retry_kit exports, with caller-supplied operations.

lanes.title: V3 · Failure boundary checks
body: Unrelated PermissionError: 1 call. Subclasses match. Empty eligibility: 1 call. Cancellation escapes.
Reuse the policy to prove invocation-local counters.

lanes.title: V4 · Installed CLI smoke
body: Today: subprocess from outside checkout expects one report line.
Proposed: same installation boundary; assert all three scenario outputs. Uses Python isolated mode.

lanes.title: V5 · Wheel rehearsal
body: Build an sdist and wheel; run the report consumer in an isolated environment using only that wheel.
Separately confirms packaging; unit checks do not establish installability.
